fields.description:
## Context

rebar's plan vocabulary carries two headings for one concept. `## Acceptance Criteria` is the
universal blocking floor: P1 (`det_floor.py`) and the standalone `check-ac` gate require a
`- [ ]` checklist with >=1 item on EVERY ticket type. `## Success Criteria` is a second heading
that the author guide asks container/epic tickets to add on top.

Investigation showed the split is vestigial vocabulary, not a live semantic axis. Every
criterion that touches them POOLS them and applies ONE bar:

- F1 opens "Examine each acceptance/success criterion for measurability and whether an agent
  can complete it within ONE working session", and its routing is
  `applies_at: {"suppress_types": ["bug"]}` — no scope restriction, so it binds containers
  exactly as it binds leaves. There is no SC carve-out.
- G3's checklist reads "The union of children covers each parent acceptance/success criterion".
- G7 fetches the parent's "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract.
- The completion verifier lists both as completion requirements.

Not one criterion applies a different bar to SC. Altitude is already carried by ROUTING — G3 is
`applies_at: {"scope": ["container"]}`, firing on whether a ticket has children — so the heading
name carries no load. The only divergence is the author guide's prose, which implies a split the
gates never implemented.

The split is also actively harmful. `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under
`## Acceptance Criteria`, resetting at the next `##`. SC is conventionally written as plain
bullets, so criteria living under SC (a) do not count toward the P1 blocking floor, (b) cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — the completion verifier matches that token only on
checkbox text, so an SC item is silently judged by the codebase bar — and (c) are not
individually checkable. Collapsing the vocabulary therefore TIGHTENS the gate.

## Why now

Renaming criteria text rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp. Until ticket
`1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` that invalidated every outstanding plan-review attestation repo-wide
(632 tickets, ~40 open/in_progress), which made this migration prohibitively expensive. ADR 0053
grandfathers registry drift at the claim gate, so the rename is now affordable.

## Scope

Collapse `## Success Criteria` into `## Acceptance Criteria` across the live vocabulary:
detector regexes, reviewer prompts, the criteria routing index, author-facing guides, the
generated criteria guide, eval specs and gold-set expectations, the test corpus, and the 108
tickets in the store that carry the old heading.

Sequenced expand-contract: detectors accept BOTH headings first, the vocabulary and data move
under that umbrella, and the alias is removed last. No window in which a ticket is
un-reviewable because its heading is in transit.

IN SCOPE: the `## Success Criteria` -> `## Acceptance Criteria` collapse and the SC -> AC
vocabulary in prompts/docs/tests, plus migrating store tickets' SC bullets to AC checkboxes.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- The `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" vocabulary — a related but SEPARATE concept
  (may be picked up as discovered work). Three live sites carry it and are excluded:
  `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`, `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`,
  and the `dod_uncertifiable` field description in `llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`.
  (AMENDED: originally written as "in the verifier prompts", which did not name the
  `verify_models.py` field carrying the identical wording.)
- `llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` — "a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria for a
  trial". Generic English about whether an EXPERIMENT succeeded, NOT the ticket heading;
  renaming it would change T2's meaning. Same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`.
  (ADDED during implementation; established by story 2aa6, whose AC6 requires it to survive.)
- Removing `clarity-check` (independently planned for removal; this epic only stops it keying
  on the SC heading).
- Frozen test fixtures that RECORD historical text (`tests/fixtures/jira/*`) and historical
  citations to a past ticket's numbered criterion.
- Anything matching `O-RAN-SC` (a Linux Foundation telecom consortium) in ADRs 0021/0022/0023
  and `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, and the minified vendor bundle
  `llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/` returns matches ONLY at the sites
      Scope excludes — `plan_review_T2.md` (trial metrics), `plan_review_verifier.md`,
      `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` and `review_kernel/verify_models.py` (all
      `dod_uncertifiable`), plus the minified vendor bundle — and NO others. Verify with
      `... | grep -v -e plan_review_T2.md -e plan_review_verifier.md
      -e plan_review_verifier_agentic.md -e verify_models.py -e editor_assets/dist/`
      returning empty.
      AMENDED: as originally written ("No live source file ... matches") this was
      UNSATISFIABLE — it contradicted this epic's own Scope, which defers the
      `dod_uncertifiable` vocabulary, and it contradicted story 2aa6's AC6, which REQUIRES
      T2's phrase to survive. The intent — no file still uses SC as the CRITERIA HEADING
      vocabulary — is unchanged and fully preserved; only the false-positive carve-outs are
      now stated, exactly as `O-RAN-SC` and the vendor bundle already were.
- [ ] Both bare-`SC` tokens meaning Success Criteria — `plan_review_G3.md:12`
      ("THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches...'") — read AC, and the
      four `O-RAN-SC` ADR/workflow occurrences are byte-identical to their pre-migration state.
- [ ] A ticket whose plan uses only `## Acceptance Criteria` passes plan review at container
      level: G3's child-coverage audit runs against the parent's AC with no criteria lost.
- [ ] EVERY store ticket carrying a `## Success Criteria` heading is migrated so its criteria
      sit under `## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items counted by
      `_count_ac_items`, proven by a post-run scan finding zero remaining SC HEADINGS (a
      backticked prose mention of the heading is not a heading and must be left intact).
      AMENDED: the set is recomputed at run time, not hard-coded — "108" was a
      point-in-time estimate. DONE: 106 tickets migrated (104 + 2 whose headings carried a
      parenthetical qualifier); 0 SC headings remain; 8 prose mentions correctly untouched.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is REGENERATED (not hand-edited) from the updated
      registry and contains EXACTLY ONE SC match — the T2 criterion's embedded prompt
      ("...stated success criteria for a trial").
      AMENDED: "contains no SC vocabulary" was unsatisfiable. The guide is a GENERATED
      snapshot of the criteria registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim, so the
      excluded T2 phrase necessarily echoes into it. Asserting exactly one match is STRICTER
      than a bare exclusion: it also proves the phrase was carried through, not dropped.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass, and every landed change
      carries `Verified +1`.
